members.title: B. Supplied-address pi Peek
members.excerpt:
### B. Supplied-address pi Peek

Input: `P`, address `n`, width `w`.  Output: `W_(n,w)(P)`.  BBP gives a genuine
remote binary/hexadecimal pi lane without preceding digits.  Plouffe's 2009
method describes a decimal lane with low memory and substantially higher time.
This is the established analogue of moving the camera while leaving the root.

members.title: 6. Scoped branches
members.excerpt:
## 6. Scoped branches

```text
Geometry (k in Z, k>=2; + in Z^2):
          U_k=(1,k), V_k=(k,1), D=(1,1), so U_k+V_k=(k+1)D.
Primes (n>=1): X_U={0,...,U-1}, pi(U-1)>=n;
          ell_n(x)=[pi(x)<n], p_n=min{x in X_U:pi(x)>=n}.
Pi (integer b>=2; m,n>=0; w>=1):
          T_n(x)=frac(b^n x); T_m(T_n(pi))=T_(m+n)(pi);
          W_(n,w)=floor(b^w T_n(pi)).
```

The first is a complementary-slope closure, the second a bounded rank-select identity, and the third a rooted navigation identity. The supported prime closure is square-frontier totality—complete primes through `B` certify trial division through `B^2`. The supported pi closure is a hash-pinned finite Pi Cell through 12 fractional digits. The rank-step and tail-camera views remain scoped candidate adapters; they do not supply physical dimension, unpaid prime certification, free pi digit content, or a remote pi-pattern locator.

members.title: Exact `35 -> 64` perpendicular rebase
members.excerpt:
## Exact `35 -> 64` perpendicular rebase

Audit07 already supplies the four endpoint views

```text
I(35)=35, O(35)=53, M(35)=64, F(35)=46,
```

where `O` reverses digits, `M` applies nines complement, and `F=O*M`.
Its historical bit chart was

```text
I=00, O=10, F=01, M=11.
```

In that chart `64` is the diagonal/antipodal view of `35`.  Rebase the same
Klein-four action using `O` and `M` as independent axes:

```text
I=00, O=10, M=01, F=11.
```

The coordinate adapter over `F_2` is

```text
(x,y)_old -> (x+y,y)_new,
```

and is its own inverse.  Under this exact `CAR`, `35 -> 64` becomes one
perpendicular complement-axis step.  No orbit member or operation changes;
only the chart does.

For clarity, future pi work should distinguish operator tags from numbers:

```text
pi[I:35]  = rooted identity view,
pi[M:64]  = nines-complement shadow view.
```

This notation does not mean `(3/5)*pi` or `(6/4)*pi`.  `pi[M:64]` remains a
dependent transformed view in the rooted pi atlas and is not automatically a
literal tail occurring elsewhere in pi.  Since `M` is an involution, the
finite-window rejoin is exact when the base-ten window convention is retained.

members.title: A. The addressed Pi `3x3`
members.excerpt:
### A. The addressed Pi `3x3`

```text
1 4 1
5 9 2
6 5 3
```

The complete frozen address is:

```text
3 | 141 | 592 | 653 | 5
```

The [finite Pi-cell receipt](../knowledge/lenses.json) proves a contextual
decoder on this pinned carrier. It is not nine unrelated digit slots. For
ordered endpoints `A<B` and code `c=(c1,c2,c3)`, the registered decoder is:

```text
D_(A,B)(c1,c2,c3) =
  [ c1      (A+B)/2     c1 ]
  [ B       A+B+c1      c2 ]
  [ B+c1    B            c3 ]
```

At `(A,B,c)=(3,5,123)` this gives exactly:

```text
[1 4 1]
[5 9 2]
[6 5 3]
```

This mechanically explains William's observation:

- the first row duplicates the first live code slot `c1=1` around endpoint
  midpoint `4`;
- the lower two rows share endpoint `B=5`;
- their other repeated relation to the first row is `6=B+c1`; and
- the center is `9=A+B+c1`.

The decoder has five typed input ports—two endpoint/context ports and three
code ports. With `(A,B)` frozen, its hot aperture is exactly the three slots
`c1,c2,c3`. Code `123` has `MANY(10)` contextual decodes when endpoints are
erased and `ONE` at endpoint context `(3,5)`.

The structural reading of the repeated rows is therefore exact. Calling the
first row SUBJECT/identity and the other rows particular identity-system roles
is still an unselected semantic adapter.

Exact occurrence facts inside the nine digits are:

- `1` occurs twice, both in the first row;
- `5` occurs twice, once in each of the other rows;
- `2,3,4,6,9` occur once; and
- `0,7,8` do not occur.

Those facts match William's “doubles” observation. They do not by themselves
select a completion rule, role dictionary, or threshold policy.
